terms.gloss: to instruct, to educate; here, to train a model
evidence: Cic. Off. 1.156: studiōsōs discendī ērudiunt atque docent (Lewis & Short)
Cic. Fam. 1.7: aliquem artibus, with the ablative of what is taught (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Classically to instruct or educate a person (see teach); used of a model it is modern, and ours. Training a model is teaching it from examples, and ērudīre takes the means in the ablative, as Cicero’s aliquem artibus ērudīre: māchinam imāginibus ērudīre. The noun is ērudītiō (see machine learning).
To instruct, train, educate (Lewis & Short), often beside ērudīre in Cicero; it also means to set up or begin, so it is less clear on its own.

phrases.english: We trained the machine on many thousands of pictures.
the data the machine is trained on; training data

sources: Lewis & Short: erudio · Lewis & Short: instituo
